name: Familial Mesial Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
aliases: Mesial Temporal Lobe Epilepsy with Hippocampal Sclerosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Familial Mesial Temporal Lobe Epilepsy

criteria.description: Recurrent focal seizures with impaired awareness originating from the mesial temporal lobe
Positive family history of mesial temporal lobe epilepsy in at least two first-degree relatives
MRI evidence of hippocampal sclerosis or mesial temporal lobe abnormalities
EEG showing epileptiform discharges localized to the mesial temporal lobe
Exclusion of other epilepsy syndromes and secondary causes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent focal seizures with impaired awareness originating from the mesial temporal lobe, positive family history in at least two first-degree relatives, and MRI evidence of hippocampal sclerosis or mesial temporal abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory; diagnosis relies on clinical, familial, and imaging data.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal impaired awareness seizures with epigastric aura
pathognomonic.notes: Typical aura includes rising epigastric sensation
searchTerms: seizures with impaired awareness and stomach aura
partial seizures with rising abdominal sensation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Automatisms such as lip-smacking or manual automatisms during seizures
searchTerms: lip-smacking or hand automatisms in seizures
repetitive mouth or hand movements during seizures

pathognomonic.symptomName: Postictal confusion lasting minutes to hours

common.symptomName: Memory impairment, particularly verbal memory deficits
Anxiety or mood disturbances related to seizure activity

searchTerms: EEG shows temporal lobe spikes between seizures
abnormal temporal brain waves when seizure-free

occasional.symptomName: Transient aphasia or speech arrest during seizures
searchTerms: temporary loss of speech during seizure

rare.symptomName: Autonomic symptoms such as pallor or flushing during seizures
searchTerms: pale or flushed skin during seizures
autonomic signs like sweating or flushing
heart rate or color changes with seizures

laboratory: Routine blood tests typically normal; used to exclude metabolic causes
imaging: MRI showing hippocampal sclerosis or mesial temporal lobe atrophy
Volumetric MRI may reveal unilateral or bilateral hippocampal volume loss
other: Video-EEG monitoring demonstrating ictal onset in mesial temporal structures

distinguishingFeatures: Similar clinical and imaging features but sporadic occurrence
Typical EEG with generalized polyspike and wave discharges
No focal temporal lobe abnormalities on MRI

redFlags: Seizures refractory to multiple antiepileptic drugs
Sudden onset of focal seizures without family history
references: Scheffer IE, Berkovic SF. The genetics of mesial temporal lobe epilepsy. Epilepsia. 2003;44 Suppl 2:29-33.
Kalviainen R, Peltola J, Partanen K, et al. Familial mesial temporal lobe epilepsy: clinical and neuroimaging features. Epilepsia. 1998;39(3):282-8.
